standard.title: Big Bang Theory and Origin of the Universe
standard.description: describe how the big bang theory models the origin and evolution of the universe and analyse the supporting evidence for the theory
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can describe Earth's position in the solar system and model day/night and seasonal cycles (AC9S6U02). They have not yet examined the universe beyond the solar system, the big bang model, or the evidence base for cosmological theory.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe the big bang theory as a model of universe origin and evolution, construct or analyse a timeline of major cosmic events, examine multiple lines of supporting evidence, and connect recent advances (gravitational waves, dark matter, SKA) to ongoing refinement of the model.

nodes.label: The big bang theory models the origin and evolution of the universe
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the big bang theory including the major stages of universe evolution from initial expansion through star and galaxy formation, and use appropriate scale units (light-years, astronomical units, scientific notation).
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe the big bang theory and construct or annotate a timeline showing at least four major stages of universe evolution.
nodes.typical_width: Students describe the big bang model of universe origin; construct a timeline from big bang through particle formation, atom formation, star formation, galaxy formation to present; describe major components of the universe (stars, galaxies, dark matter, dark energy) using appropriate units; and explain how stars' light spectra reveal composition, movement and distance.
wider: Research First Nations Australians' knowledges of celestial bodies and explanations of the origin of the universe — comparing with the big bang model as different knowledge frameworks for explaining the same phenomena
Explore recent advances including gravitational wave detection, dark matter and dark energy discoveries, and how these have expanded our understanding (AC9S10H02)
Examine how the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder enables collection of astronomical data at unprecedented scale — connecting technology to knowledge advance (AC9S10H02)
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 (evidence for the big bang) requires students to evaluate specific evidence types — red shift, CMB, Hubble's observations — against the model. Students who do not have a clear timeline and sequence of the big bang model cannot evaluate what each piece of evidence supports or why it matters. The model must precede the evidence examination.

response_modes.reason: The timeline of universe evolution — from initial expansion through particle formation, atom formation, star and galaxy formation — must be explicit before students can evaluate what each piece of evidence supports. Without this sequence as a reference frame, students cannot reason about why red shift or CMB radiation matters to the model.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations cosmological knowledge provides a valuable comparative direction that respects both knowledge systems without conflating them. Recent advances (gravitational waves, dark matter) provide genuinely exciting enrichment connecting the theory to frontier science.
success_criteria: Describes the big bang theory and the major stages of universe evolution in sequence
Uses appropriate scale units (light-years, scientific notation) when describing the universe

nodes.label: Multiple lines of evidence support the big bang theory
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe multiple independent lines of evidence for the big bang theory and explain what each contributes to support for the model.
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe at least three lines of evidence for the big bang and explain what each shows.
nodes.typical_width: Students examine cosmic microwave background radiation, red/blue shift of galaxies, Hubble's observations, and the proportion of matter in the universe as independent lines of evidence; explain what each contributes; and explain how the discovery of gravitational waves validated Einstein's general relativity 100 years after prediction — connecting evidence accumulation to theory refinement (AC9S10H01).
wider: Examine how each type of evidence — CMB radiation, red shift, Hubble's observations, matter proportions — independently supports the big bang and how they converge

Explore why the discovery of gravitational waves validated Einstein's general relativity — examining how a prediction made 100 years earlier was eventually confirmed by technology not yet available (AC9S10H01)
Identify different technologies used to collect astronomical data and the specific evidence types each enables
success_criteria: Names at least three lines of evidence for the big bang and explains what each contributes
Explains how converging independent evidence strengthens a scientific theory
